SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.25
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows three strong C–H stretching bands at 2877, 2932 and 2964 cm⁻¹, typical of an aliphatic R-CH₃/R-CH₂ system.  
Key functional-group clues are the set 1664 cm⁻¹, 1341 cm⁻¹ and 826 cm⁻¹.  Alkyl nitrites (R-O–N=O) characteristically give a strong N=O stretch near 1660–1670 cm⁻¹, a symmetric N–O stretch around 1320–1350 cm⁻¹ and an N–O bending (δ(NO–N–O)) mode close to 800–830 cm⁻¹ (rule GFQ-022).  All three are present here (1664, 1341, 826 cm⁻¹), strongly indicating an alkyl nitrite.  

Among the candidates only molecules 1 (CCCCON=O, n-butyl nitrite) and 7 (isopropyl nitrite) contain the O–N=O grouping.  The spectrum also contains a CH₂ rocking band near 915 cm⁻¹, which favours the n-butyl chain (three CH₂ groups) of candidate 1 over the more branched isopropyl chain in candidate 7.  Hence candidate 1 best matches both the functional-group and chain-type features of the observed Raman peaks.
